title: Six Laredo ISD JROTC Cadets Named Honorable Cadets for Leadership and Service
excerpt: Six Laredo Independent School District JROTC students were named Honorable Cadets at a ceremony at Nixon High School, honored for service, self-discipline, resp
content:
Six Laredo Independent School District JROTC students were named Honorable Cadets at a ceremony at Nixon High School, honored for service, self-discipline, responsibility and respect.

The six are Jose Gonzalez and Robert Ibarra of Martin High School; Cig Valeria Hernandez and Jacqueline Tapia of Cigarroa High School; and Amaris Izaguirre and Briana Morales of Nixon High School.

The recognition is run by the LISD JROTC Program and the LISD College, Career and Military Readiness Department. To be selected, cadets complete an application and resume, submit two recommendation letters from outside JROTC and one from a JROTC instructor, write an essay and earn a cadet challenge score.

Gonzalez, of Martin, is a National Honor Society member. He has enlisted in the Marine Corps and will attend boot camp in San Diego, and plans to take college courses during active duty and earn a Business degree.

Ibarra, also of Martin, runs on the Martin track team. He plans to earn an associate degree in criminal justice, then join the Army, with a goal of working for U.S. Customs.

Hernandez, of Cigarroa, is on the Toro Cheer team, national champions two years running, and also performs with the Diamond Dolls. She plans to earn a Criminal Justice degree and pursue a law-enforcement career.

Tapia, also of Cigarroa, is a student at Sabas Perez Early College High School as well. She plans to enlist in the Navy, then pursue law enforcement.

Izaguirre, of Nixon, is a National Honor Society member, part of Communities in Schools, and a member of the Vidal M. Treviño School of Communications and Fine Arts all-female Conjunto Group. She plans to attend Laredo College and Texas A&M International University, majoring in Criminal Justice.

Morales, also of Nixon, won her first National Award at the annual cadet awards ceremony. She is Raider XO and Color Guard leader, and she owns her own crochet business. She plans to earn a Criminal Justice degree at TAMIU, with a goal of working for U.S. Customs.

At the ceremony, the Nixon High School JROTC presented the colors, and a barbecue lunch was prepared by Nixon Culinary Arts students, directed by Grizelda Sauceda Madrigal and Michelle Crawford. Brisket was provided by Meat Processing and FFA teachers Aucenio Lopez and Reynaldo Garza.

For more information about the LISD JROTC Honorable Cadet program, contact Mayra Garcia with the LISD College, Career and Military Readiness Department at 956-273-1863.
